metaTitle: Space ETF Guide: Which Space ETFs Hold SpaceX?
metaDescription: Compare space ETF options holding SpaceX stock (SPCX). See weights, fees, and holdings for UFO, ARKX, NASA, and ROKT to pick the right fund.
h1: Space ETF Options with SpaceX Exposure
cardBlurb: Compare which space ETFs hold SpaceX stock, review their portfolio weights, and calculate your effective dollar exposure.
introText:
Three exchange-traded fund (ETF) choices hold listed SpaceX stock among their top positions: UFO, ARKX, and NASA. A fourth fund, ROKT, does not list SpaceX in its top ten holdings. 

SpaceX began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX on June 12, 2026. The initial public offering (IPO) priced 555,555,555 Class A shares at $135 per share. With a 52-week trading range of $104.83 to $225.64 and a recent close of $146.03 on October 16, 2026, stock prices shift every trading day. You can review current share pricing directly through [SPCX on Stock Analysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/spcx/).

 If you want to know how individual stock purchases differ, check our guide on [how to buy SpaceX stock](/guides/how-to-buy-spacex-stock/). Here is how the primary funds allocate your capital across SpaceX and competing aerospace holdings.

sections.heading: Which Space ETFs Hold SpaceX?
sections.body:
The choice among space ETF options depends on whether you want high SpaceX concentration or broad aerospace exposure. As of mid-October 2026, per fund data reported by Stock Analysis, Procure Space ETF (UFO), ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX), and Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA) allocate significant portfolio weights to SpaceX. SPDR S&P Kensho Final Frontiers ETF (ROKT) does not list SpaceX among its ten largest positions.

| Ticker | Fund Name | Issuer | Expense Ratio | SPCX Weight | Largest Other Holdings | Fits If You Want |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UFO | Procure Space ETF | ProcureAM | 0.75% | 16.05% | Trimble, Garmin, EchoStar, Sirius XM, Rocket Lab | Largest listed SPCX allocation |
| ARKX | ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF | ARK | 0.75% | 11.16% | L3Harris, Deere, Kratos, NVIDIA, Rocket Lab | Active management with defense and enterprise tech |
| NASA | Tema Space Innovators ETF | Tema | 0.75% | 9.06% direct (plus 17.94% SPV) | Rocket Lab, AST SpaceMobile, Viasat, Filtronic | Maximum exposure to SpaceX equity and private vehicles |
| ROKT | SPDR S&P Kensho Final Frontiers ETF | State Street | 0.45% | Not in top 10 | Forum Energy Technologies, Oceaneering, Ducommun, RTX | Lower-cost broader aerospace mix |

Procure Space ETF, trading as [UFO on Stock Analysis](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/ufo/), maintains SPCX as its largest holding at 16.05%. Its other top positions include Trimble at 5.49%, Garmin at 5.37%, EchoStar at 4.84%, Sirius XM at 4.81%, and Rocket Lab at 4.57%. Together, its top ten holdings represent 55.82% of fund assets.

ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF, tracked as [ARKX on Stock Analysis](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/arkx/), holds SPCX as its largest individual position at 11.16%. Because it is an actively managed fund, ARKX also holds defense and technology companies. Its portfolio includes L3Harris at 6.55%, Deere at 5.67%, Kratos at 5.48%, NVIDIA at 5.34%, Rocket Lab at 4.98%, and Amazon at 4.79%, with the top ten accounting for 57.16% of total assets.

Tema Space Innovators ETF, found as [NASA on Stock Analysis](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/nasa/), splits its position into two lines. It holds listed SPCX stock at 9.06% and carries a separate position labeled SpaceX SPV Exposure (Common) at 17.94%. This represents an indirect holding through a special-purpose vehicle. Other top positions include Rocket Lab at 9.46% and AST SpaceMobile at 5.92%, with its top ten assets reaching 67.45%.

SPDR S&P Kensho Final Frontiers ETF, listed as [ROKT on Stock Analysis](https://stockanalysis.com/etf/rokt/), takes a different approach. Its top ten positions comprise 38.10% of the portfolio and do not include SPCX. Instead, its primary holdings include Forum Energy Technologies at 4.50%, Oceaneering at 4.04%, Ducommun at 4.02%, RTX at 3.96%, and Lockheed Martin at 3.82%.

sections.heading: Dollar Exposure per Thousand Invested
sections.body:
Every dollar you place into an exchange-traded fund gets split according to the portfolio weights of the underlying securities. An ETF holds a basket of securities where buying one share gives you exposure to every holding in proportion to its published weight. The regulatory framework for these pooled products is detailed by [Investor.gov on mutual funds and ETFs](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-1).

If you invest $1,000 into Procure Space ETF (UFO) at its mid-October 2026 weight of 16.05%, you purchase approximately $160.50 of SpaceX exposure. The remaining $839.50 is spread across satellite radio providers, navigation hardware makers, and launch contractors such as Rocket Lab.

A $1,000 investment in ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX) at an 11.16% allocation gives you roughly $111.60 of SpaceX stock. The remaining $888.40 goes to defense equipment manufacturers like L3Harris and Kratos, agriculture equipment makers like Deere, and enterprise tech firms like NVIDIA and Alphabet.

A $1,000 allocation to Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA) yields about $90.60 in listed SPCX shares based on its 9.06% listed position. When you factor in the 17.94% special-purpose vehicle position, the combined direct and indirect SpaceX allocation equals approximately $270.00. You can test how regular contributions build over time by using our free [investment calculator](/investing/).

For ROKT, because SPCX is absent from the published top ten, whether a $1,000 buy provides direct SpaceX exposure is not shown. Instead, the bulk of your capital funds its broader holdings mix.

sections.heading: Concentration vs Broad Aerospace Exposure
sections.body:
Portfolio concentration determines how closely your returns track a single business versus the broader aerospace economy. When an ETF concentrates more than half its assets in ten companies, poor performance from two or three holdings will drag down your entire position. Investors evaluating heavy individual weightings should review the risks explained in our guide to [concentrated stock position risk](/guides/concentrated-stock-position-risk/).

Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA) carries the heaviest concentration among the group, with 67.45% of its portfolio in its top ten holdings. If you combine its listed SPCX stock and its SPV position, SpaceX represents 27.00% of the entire fund. This gives investors significant exposure to SpaceX equity and indirect SPV holdings.

 Its top ten holdings make up 55.82% of assets, including Rocket Lab, Viasat, and Globalstar. 

ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX) is an actively managed fund that also holds defense and technology companies. Its top ten concentration stands at 57.16%, holding companies such as AeroVironment, AMD, and Amazon. ROKT offers the lowest top ten concentration at 38.10%, spreading assets across its broader aerospace mix.

To understand how exchange-traded baskets compare against traditional pooled products, read our breakdown of [ETF vs mutual fund](/compare/etf-vs-mutual-fund/) structures.

sections.heading: Expense Ratios and Annual Holding Costs
sections.body:
An expense ratio represents the annual fee an ETF issuer deducts from fund assets to cover management, operations, and administration. This fee is not billed directly to your brokerage balance; instead, it reduces the net asset value of the fund on an ongoing basis.

Three of the primary space funds charge an identical expense ratio of 0.75% per year:

- Procure Space ETF (UFO): 0.75%
- ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX): 0.75%
- Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA): 0.75%

On a $1,000 balance, an expense ratio of 0.75% costs exactly $7.50 annually. On a $10,000 portfolio, this management fee equals $75.00 each year. If you hold $50,000 across these funds, you pay $375.00 annually in fund overhead.

SPDR S&P Kensho Final Frontiers ETF (ROKT) carries a lower expense ratio of 0.45%. On a $1,000 balance, ROKT costs $4.50 per year. That represents an annual savings of $3.00 per $1,000 invested compared to UFO, ARKX, or NASA. 

Lower fees do not automatically make ROKT the superior option if your goal is holding SpaceX. Because ROKT does not list SPCX in its top ten holdings, choosing it strictly for its 0.45% fee may not deliver the SpaceX exposure you are targeting. For an analysis of how passive tracking compares to index mechanics, see our overview of [index fund vs ETF](/compare/index-fund-vs-etf/) investing.

sections.heading: ETF Tradeoffs vs Direct SPCX Stock
sections.body:
Investors must choose between buying single shares of SPCX or purchasing an ETF that holds SpaceX alongside dozens of peers. Each route has distinct operational mechanics and risk profiles.

Buying SPCX stock directly delivers pure 100% exposure to SpaceX operations. You pay no management fees or annual expense ratios to an intermediary fund manager. However, owning single-company equity concentrates your entire capital balance into one stock.

Buying a space ETF spreads your capital across a basket of securities in proportion to their weights. You also gain automated rebalancing, as the fund issuer handles corporate actions and adjusts weights periodically. In exchange for this diversification, you pay an annual expense ratio of 0.45% to 0.75%, and your returns will be diluted by lagging holdings in the basket.

When buying individual shares or thematic ETFs through a brokerage account, review order types to manage trading costs. Read the official guidance from [Investor.gov on market orders](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/market-order) and the protections provided by [Investor.gov on limit orders](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/limit-order). If you are investing smaller dollar balances, you can also explore fractional purchasing through [Investor.gov on fractional share investing](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/fractional-share-investing).

sections.heading: Can You Hold Space ETFs in Trump Accounts?
sections.body:
A federal Trump Account cannot hold space ETFs or individual shares of SPCX. Under federal rules established for these child savings vehicles, account balances may only be invested in one low-cost index fund that tracks the S&P 500 or a similar broad U.S. stock index. Parents cannot purchase UFO, ARKX, NASA, ROKT, or any single corporate security inside the program.

 On Monday, October 19, 2026, Elon Musk posted on X that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America, calling it the first of many. According to coverage from [CNN on Musk's SpaceX post](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/19/business/elon-musk-children-spacex-shares-x-post-intl), Musk framed the gift as a way to encourage interest in space and investing. Coverage from [Axios on the SpaceX pledge](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/19/elon-musk-spacex-shares-kids) and reporting from [IBTimes on the child share proposal](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/elon-musk-reportedly-plans-give-105-billion-spacex-shares-every-single-us-child-1826413) noted that about 72 million kids live in the United States, valuing the pledge at roughly $10.5 billion to $11 billion depending on the share price used.

Musk did not establish a claim form, application website, or age cutoff, nor did he confirm whether Trump Accounts would serve as the distribution vehicle. Read our analysis of [Elon Musk's SpaceX share for kids](/guides/elon-musk-spacex-share-for-kids/) for complete background. Earlier in July 2026, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell pledged shares to Trump Accounts for about two million children, as covered by [The Next Web on Shotwell's pledge](https://thenextweb.com/news/shotwell-spacex-stock-trump-accounts).

Federal rules published in the [Federal Register on Trump Account regulations](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/30/2026-20026/trump-accounts) under T.D. 10056 state that individuals cannot donate stock directly to a specific child's account. Corporate donations must route through eligible 501(c)(3) charities and distribute equally across a qualified class. The [Treasury press release SB-0642](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0642) confirmed that automatic enrollment was completed October 1, 2026. Account claims are processed at [TrumpAccounts.gov](https://trumpaccounts.gov) and the [IRS Trump Accounts page](https://www.irs.gov/trumpaccounts).

If you want to build a portfolio of space ETFs or individual SPCX shares for a child, you must open a private account outside the federal system. Read our tutorial on [how to open a custodial brokerage account for kids](/guides/how-to-open-a-custodial-brokerage-account-for-kids/) to set up a standard custodial structure that supports thematic funds.

sections.heading: How to Verify Fund Holdings Before Investing
sections.body:
Portfolio weights inside exchange-traded funds fluctuate every business day based on market moves, inflows, and redemptions. The weights published across financial websites often differ depending on when each platform refreshes its portfolio data. For instance, mid-June 2026 media reports listed UFO's SpaceX allocation near 6%, whereas mid-October 2026 data shows the position at 16.05%.

Before placing an order for any space ETF, check current portfolio allocations. Verify whether SPCX remains a top holding and check whether the fund holds listed common stock or indirect special-purpose vehicles.

Check the bid-ask spread on your trading platform before entering an order. Using a limit order ensures you never execute a trade at a price higher than your stated maximum. Once you confirm the current holdings and pricing, submit your order through your brokerage account.

faqs.question: Which is the best space ETF?
faqs.answer: No single fund is the best option for every investor because each portfolio targets a different strategy. Procure Space ETF (UFO) holds a 16.05% SpaceX weighting alongside holdings like Trimble and Garmin. ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX) fits those wanting active management across defense and tech. Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA) offers the highest combined SpaceX exposure, while SPDR S&P Kensho Final Frontiers ETF (ROKT) delivers the lowest expense ratio at 0.45%.

faqs.question: Is SpaceX in the UFO ETF?
faqs.answer: Yes, SpaceX (SPCX) is the largest holding in Procure Space ETF (UFO). As of mid-October 2026, it represents 16.05% of the fund's total assets, followed by holdings in Trimble, Garmin, EchoStar, and Rocket Lab.

faqs.question: Does NASA ETF have SpaceX?
faqs.answer: Yes, Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA) holds SpaceX in two separate positions. It holds listed SPCX common stock at a 9.06% weighting and holds a SpaceX SPV Exposure position at 17.94%, giving it a combined direct and indirect allocation of 27.00%.

faqs.question: What ETF will have SpaceX?
faqs.answer: SpaceX is currently held by Procure Space ETF (UFO), ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX), and Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA). SPDR S&P Kensho Final Frontiers ETF (ROKT) does not list SPCX in its top ten holdings.

faqs.question: Can I put a space ETF in my child's Trump Account?
faqs.answer: No, federal Trump Accounts cannot hold thematic ETFs, space funds, or single stocks like SPCX. Under federal program regulations, Trump Accounts can only be invested in one low-cost index fund tracking the S&P 500 or a similar broad U.S. stock index. To hold space ETFs for a minor, you must open a standard custodial brokerage account.
